audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The coding (fixed-dominant, rule 01 101 0101 10101 = primary on ultima, secondary on antepenult, alternating leftward) rests on the only reference grammar of the language, Wivell 1981 (MA thesis, 231 pp), whose stress section I opened at p. 27 / sec. 2.2.1.1: the quotation is verbatim (modulo the scanned artefact 'antipenultirna' for 'antipenultima'), and the accompanying schema (((S5) S4) S̀3) S2 Ś1 and transcribed 2-5 syllable examples match the rule string exactly. A second source by the same author, the SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (fetched sources now from Wayback), independently states 'Primarily stress falls upon the last syllable.' Glottolog's full 10-item bibliography, Crossref and Semantic Scholar show no later phonology, prosody or instrumental work, and the Ross 2002 sketch is derivative of Wivell. So the record is well-sourced; the only defects are bookkeeping: grade field empty

sources.citation: Wivell 1981 Kairiru Grammar, sec 2.2.1.1, full PDF via Wayback (sil.org reapdata, snap 20180808)
sources.quote: Word stress is placed as follows: Primary stress falls upon the ultima, secondary stress on the antipenultirna and so on.

sources.quote: Word stress is placed as follows: Primary stress falls upon the ultima, secondary stress on the antipenultima and so on. (((S5) S4) S̀3) S2 Ś1; e.g. [mìs·i·síu] /misisiu/ 'hiccough', [ša·rèm·pa·rém] /jaremparem/ 'threadfin fish', [r̃a·kuk·ù·ra·kái] /r̃akukuraqai/ 'they come together'. 2.2.1.2: in a complex vowel nucleus stress falls on the first vowel of the sequence.
